Early Chinese Coin Finds Database

Overview

A research tool, not just a dataset

The database catalogues archaeological discoveries of pre-Qin to early Han coinage across China. Every record links a find site to its geographic location, archaeological context, coin typology, and bibliographic sources — queryable directly from Supabase, with a handful of stable reference datasets (mint-town dossiers, typology hierarchy) kept local for anything that rarely changes.

Search

Full-text and faceted search

Every find site is searchable by name, province, coin type, inscription, or site code, with facet filters for region, period, site type, coin type, state, mint, and quantity — plus a live results map and a per-site coin-type pie chart.

  • Sortable by name, quantity, region, find count, coin-type diversity, or state diversity
  • Location-precision filter (site / county / city / all) with a click-to-explain badge on "All," since it deliberately surfaces real gaps in geolocation precision rather than hiding them
Site Records

One page per archaeological find

Location, coin types found, excavation contexts, individual finds, a mint-origins map connecting the site to every mint it received coins from, and full bibliographic sources — all in one record.

Mints

Every documented coin-producing town

A searchable, sortable directory of mint towns — merging live database rows with hand-transcribed dossiers (location, description, images, citations) wherever the database doesn't carry a field yet, and clearly flagging which is which.

  • Sort by number of finds, number of coins, number of catalogued issues, or completeness of the record
  • Static, English-only reference data is visually distinguished (dashed border) from live, bilingual database data — never silently mixed
Mint Detail

Location, coin output, and primary sources

Each mint's own page: coordinates on a detail map, an issued-coin distribution map (filterable by coin type), an image gallery for historical city plans, and full bilingual citations back to the original excavation reports.

Coin Types

The full typology, browsable end to end

Every documented coin type as a searchable card grid and a full expandable hierarchy tree (钱币/Coin and 钱范/Mould branches), each card showing obverse/reverse photography where available, sortable by hierarchy level, find count, coin count, or catalogued issues.

Coin Type Detail

One typology node, fully cross-referenced

Obverse/reverse images, parent types, every issuing state and mint, every attested inscription, a collapsible coin-issue catalogue, related find sites, and this node's place in the overall hierarchy tree.

Map Visualizations

Three ways to see the same geography

Find Site, Mint Town, and Museum Collections all share one full-bleed map engine with Points / Density / Compare display modes — click-to-reveal explanations on every non-obvious control (View by, Filter by, Display) so the interface teaches itself.

Find Site
Every findspot, filterable by coin type or mint, colored by match ratio.
Mint Town
Every mint town, sized and colored by output — database-backed.
Museum Collections
ANS specimens shown the same way, plus accession-number search.
About the Project

Documentation-first, bilingual by design

Project scope, database schema, and team live on a dedicated About page — every string in the UI is a translation-table lookup, never a hardcoded literal, so the entire site re-renders in Chinese with one toggle.

Architecture

Server components, one remote datastore

No separate backend or API layer: React Server Components query Supabase directly at render time. A small set of local, rarely-changing reference files (mint dossiers, river overlays, specimen photography) supplements the database wherever it doesn't carry a field yet — and the UI always makes clear which is which.
